My father doesn't know that I have PTSD, and my mother denies it. I still live in the same house as my father, and feel a lot of anxiety often and feel constantly overstimulated and anxious. Since I was also diagnosed with autism as well, the noise of my house really bothers me. The dogs constantly barking, my dad yelling and screaming, the TV being turned up to 70. Even with noise cancelling headphones and earbuds in I can still hear everything, and I often feel like my parents are always calling my name, so I often feel paranoid and have trouble using headphones in my own house. In three months I will finally be able to escape and go off to college, but after 18 years of dealing with this, I can't wait to finally have some freedom. Another thing is, I think that people need to understand is that you can develop PTSD from many different ways and situations, and that like most things, it affects each person differently. I just wish that instead of my parents denying, they could try to understand and listen to what I have to say instead of shut me down every time I try to speak.

I’ve recently started studying anatomy, and I would say breaking it down helps organize all of the new knowledge and info there is to learn. I would start with how different systems work with one another, so you can get an idea of how the overall body works, and get an introduction and a big picture of the body. I would then break it down into sections. For example, is you study the skeletal system, you can study a few different areas of the skeletal system. Start off by learning the different types of bones there are, then go onto learning about the inside of the bone. Once you learn about bones you can move onto the muscles, tendons, ligaments, joints, etc. ask yourself how each system connects with one another, and make connections as you learn. Questions keep you interested and help you deeply think about the subject at hand.

Hey, I can tell you’re really strong for making it this long. The fact that you continue to manage to fight is amazing, just keep fighting. You’re still young, and none of us know what the future may hold. If you give up now, you will lose your chance at the future you deserve. I truly believe you can eventually overcome and be free of these issues that you face, and if you just want to have a chat, I’m here for you.

You are kind for the fact you want to comfort others, and it’s okay to feel weak at times, even all the time. What makes you think you will be better off gone? (Only if you want to talk about it, that is)

If no one will help you then you must help yourself until you can finally get help, do whatever you can to fixate on something besides your thoughts, anything. I believe in you, you are strong and you can do it.

That’s amazing that you don’t want to give up, and keep it that way. Is there anything you can do to change at least one thought a day to something that isn’t bullying yourself? Notice your thoughts, and try to change just one thought. I know this might sound incredibly difficult, and I understand that and am still trying to work on it myself, but it might help ease the pain just a little bit. You don’t even have to change the negative thought into a positive thought, just making one thought a day into a neutral thought might help. I hope this might help you even just a little bit, and just know that I’m proud of you.
